misconception_description: Student believes that in the expression x == a or b, the comparison operator distributes to both operands of the or operator.

solutions.generated_code:
program HitungPasanganTidakSama
kamus
  a, b, c, jumlah : integer
algoritma
  input(a, b, c)
  jumlah <- 0
  if a != b or c then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if a != c or c then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  if b != c or c then
    jumlah <- jumlah + 1
  endif
  output(jumlah)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student modified the condition from `if (arr[i] != arr[j])` to `if (arr[i] != arr[j] or j)`. The student believes this distributes the comparison operator, interpreting it as checking if arr[i] is not equal to arr[j] OR not equal to j (the index). However, this actually evaluates as `(arr[i] != arr[j]) or j`, where `j` is an integer that will be truthy for all values in the loop (since j >= 1). This causes the condition to always be True, making the function incorrectly count ALL pairs instead of only unequal pairs. The student thinks they're adding an additional check for inequality, but they're actually breaking the logic entirely.
